note: Influence and approval are gameplay starting values for 1 January 2000, not measured data. With no central government, power lay with clan-based armed factions and militias (modelled as 'military'), clan elders and pastoralist communities ('rural'), Mogadishu merchants and the remittance and telecom businesses ('business'), and clerics and local Islamic courts ('religious_establishment'). Approval is of the national political order, which was absent, so it is low across the board.

interest_groups.note: No national army existed; this group stands for clan militias and faction forces.
No national police or intelligence service was functioning.
Mogadishu traders, remittance (hawala) companies and private telecoms.
Clerics and the local Islamic courts that provided justice in parts of Mogadishu.
Clan elders and pastoralist and farming communities.
Bantu (Jareer), Benadiri and other minority groups outside the main clan families.
Private newspapers and radio stations, mainly in Mogadishu.
